newsitem.title: ISRAEL: PLO corruption probe implicates five ministers.
newsitem.headline: PLO corruption probe implicates five ministers.

text.p: A Palestinian Authority official said on Sunday five ministers were implicated in a report that found the self-rule government had misused $326 million in public funds last year.

"Five ministers were named in the report as violators and were accused of mismanagement and squandering of public funds," the official, who spoke on condition he not be named, told Reuters. He did not identify the ministers.

An auditing office set up by Palestinian President Yasser Arafat said on Saturday the self-rule government in the West Bank and Gaza had misused $326 million in public funds in the period December 1995 to December 1996.
The 600-page report by the Authority's Monitoring Institution was the first official charge of corruption within the administration since self-rule began in 1994.
Tayeb Abdel-Rahim, General Secretary of the Palestinian Presidency, told Reuters on Sunday: "President Arafat has decided to follow up the report by the monitoring institution.

"He has set up a high-level committee and instructed the committee members to carry out investigations against violations mentioned in the report. The committee will recommend steps to put an end to violations and squandering of public funds."

Monitoring Institution chief Jarrar al-Qudwa told Reuters on Saturday the report, a copy of which was handed to Arafat, found that "around" $326 million had been mismanaged or squandered. He said the report had not been made public yet.

Qudwa's comments coincided with increasing complaints by Palestinians and their elected representatives in the Palestinian Legislative Council of corruption by cabinet officials and government employees.
Palestinian lawmakers on Wednesday charged the Palestinian Authority was using taxpayers' money on villas and cars for ministers and other senior officials.

Qudwa said the Authority's losses from mismanaging funds for projects and improper distribution of state land were estimated at $67 million. He did not say if any of the mismanaged money came from donations from foreign states.
"Our report mentions some officials by name who have given certain companies projects to work on because they have personal interests with those companies," Qudwa told Voice of Palestine radio.
He said his report would be made public soon.
"Any money that is spent without the permission of the Finance Ministry is money squandered," he said.

Finance Minister Mohammad Zuhdi al-Nashashibi acknowledged last week that several companies in the Gaza Strip and the West Bank had not paid taxes. He also said reform was needed in Palestinian Authority ministries.
